subject.title: fix(shared): cap backtick delimiter length to prevent unbounded repeat

question: Should pathological Markdown payloads be rejected or limited before these shared formatters, or should the formatters adopt a cross-renderer-safe alternate representation when no bounded delimiter exists?
rationale: No fixed backtick cap can represent every possible payload while preserving both inline and fenced containment, and choosing rejection versus alternate encoding changes shared caller behavior.

options.title: Bound input before formatting
options.body: Keep the existing containment-preserving formatter contract and reject or truncate oversized payloads at the owning caller before Markdown generation.

options.title: Define an alternate encoding
options.body: Specify and test a renderer-compatible non-backtick representation for payloads whose safe delimiter would exceed the resource limit.

options.title: Allow an explicit formatter error
options.body: Change the helpers to return a typed failure for pathological inputs and update every caller to handle that outcome.

recommendation.title: Bound input before formatting
recommendation.body: Keep the existing containment-preserving formatter contract and reject or truncate oversized payloads at the owning caller before Markdown generation.

likelyOwner.reason: This cross-caller shared-formatting contract needs a core ownership decision, and this is the best available repository-level routing candidate.
